case: MariaDB app keyed-grid edits preserve explicit empty ENUM and SET values under EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL
engine: MariaDB 11 and MySQL Docker integration fixtures

behavior_before_fix.result: MariaDB native keyed-grid edit stored both explicit empty ENUM and SET values as SQL NULL under EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL.
behavior_before_fix.test_delta: The mode cases were added to the existing app contract before the baseline run; the production keyed-update builder was unchanged.

fix: The shared MySQL keyed-update builder emits SPACE(0) for an empty Value::Text assigned to an ENUM or SET column. Empty text assigned to ordinary text columns remains a bound parameter.
contract: The MariaDB app parser distinguishes blank input, which means SQL NULL, from explicit empty input, which means empty ENUM or zero-member SET.
Under EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL alone and combined with STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, ANSI_QUOTES, and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, native ordinal, byte, null-state, and sibling-row checks preserve both meanings.
The existing MySQL grid-edit contract passes across its twelve SQL mode combinations with the same SQL expression generation.
A core SQL-builder test confirms typed ENUM/SET empty values use SPACE(0), while ordinary text remains bound and primary-key parameters stay correctly ordered.
